exposure: payment of prenatal and childbirth by the Unified Health System
cohort: 1,295 women who gave birth in Botucatu, Sao Paulo, Brazil, in the first semester of 2012.
finding: Socio-demographic factors (age >= 18 years, >= high school education, paid work, and living with a partner) and receiving prenatal care through the supplementary health network were independently associated with increased odds of elective cesarean section.
mod_finding: Women with better socio-economic conditions were more likely to have an elective cesarean section.
